title: The Volunteer Shift Nobody at the Office Knows About
script: Narrator: [reflective] Twice a week, before the sun has fully risen, I cook breakfast for a shelter that houses women who have nowhere else to go, and almost nobody at my office has the faintest idea this is how I spend those mornings.

Narrator: [thoughtful] It isn't that I've deliberately concealed it, exactly; it's more that whenever the subject drifts anywhere close, I find a way to steer the conversation elsewhere, almost instinctively.
Narrator: [honestly] Last month, a journalist who was writing a feature on community kitchens somehow tracked me down, having heard about the shift from one of the shelter's coordinators.
Narrator: [with feeling] She wanted a photograph, a short interview, my name printed beside a headline about quiet acts of kindness that go unnoticed in the city.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Part of me, I'll admit, was flattered, which surprised me more than the offer itself did, given how little I usually crave that sort of attention.
Narrator: [reflective] If the article had run, colleagues who currently assume I'm simply bad at replying to early morning messages would have finally understood where I disappear to.
Narrator: [honestly] Even so, the more I pictured my face in print, the more uneasy I became, as though something I'd been doing quietly was about to be repurposed into something performed.
Narrator: [determined] So I turned the offer down, and suggested she interview the shelter's founder instead, since the kitchen would not exist at all without her tireless effort.
Narrator: [sincere] I don't say this to suggest that nobody should ever be photographed doing good; plenty of good is done publicly for perfectly good reasons.
Narrator: [thoughtful] For me specifically, though, I've noticed that the moment an act starts feeling like it's being witnessed, some quieter, purer version of my intention starts slipping away.
Narrator: [reflective] I'd rather keep this particular habit small and unremarkable, something between myself, the tired women eating breakfast, and whoever it is I'm ultimately doing it for.
Narrator: [peacefully] So the shifts continue, unmentioned and unphotographed, and if my coworkers ever do find out, I suspect it won't be from me.
